newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mixed, partly follows heat.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mixed, partly follows heat.

text.p: North American bunker prices were mixed in moderate trade amid weaker prices abroad, average demand and several other factors, players said on Thursday.
In the East Coast, New York Harbor prices fell about $10 since Tuesday following the resupply midweek of several players.

"Avails have finally lined up. For awhile they were pretty tight," said one Harbor trader, adding the decline in heating oil futures and prices in Europe have also put downward pressure on the market.
Spot 380 CST in the Harbor traded between $133 and $134 a tonne, about $9 below Tuesday levels. 180 CST also fell $9 to $140/143, traders said.
On the Gulf Coast, Houston 380 CST fell $13 in quiet activity to $117/118, with 180 CST following, trading at $120/121.
The West Coast finally pulled out of its nearly four week stall, rising up on congestion problems in some ports and problems of resupply.
In Los Angeles, 380 CST moved up $6 to $122/123 and 180 CST rose to $127/128.
Players said demand was light but resupply for Chemoil had been delayed so there was not much choice for supply.
"The numbers will probably come back down soon," said one Los Angeles trader.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
